items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Monk came into the rehearsal and sat at the chair and we started to run down the arrangements... It was a disaster rehearsal.

ctx.x: Excuse me for interrupting again, Cliff. But I think for the record we might as well let them know that the studio you were rehearsing in was Eddie Barefield who was a saxophone player. And the piano player - and Ken Kersey was a pianist so they would know who Ken Kersey was -- he was a pianist, the late Ken Kersey, and of course, everybody knows he played piano. Please carry on.

However, I have to say first, as we went to the rehearsal, he hadn't hired Kenny yet, and we rehearsed first without Kenny and somebody suggested that Monk --Thelonius Monk -- was at Minton's and he was out for awhile and he could use a job.

I had heard Monk play on the street, but I didn't say anything to Ben because I didn't know whether he'd fit in this combination. However, Monk came into the rehearsal and sat at the chair and we started to run down the arrangements, and Monk listened. And so Ben would stop the band and say to play some chords, and Monk thought it over, and he'd lean on one elbow and poke a couple of notes. It was a disaster rehearsal. And Ben was pretty upset.
